title: Data Drift, Concept Drift, Decay: MLOps

scenes.line1: Why do models fail in production?
scenes.line2: Can you spot the warning signs?
scenes.say: Why do machine learning models break after deployment? Can you catch the early warning signs before users notice?

scenes.label: Drift
scenes.sub: Data drift is when input data changes over time.
scenes.say: First up, data drift. This happens when the distribution of your input data shifts compared to what your model saw during training.
Data drift is about changing inputs. Concept drift is sneakier—the relationship between features and labels shifts, even if the data looks the same.

scenes.title: Detecting Drift & Decay
scenes.say: You can run a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to catch data drift. If your accuracy drops from ninety-two percent to eighty-five, that's performance decay.

scenes.question: If accuracy drops, what do you do?
scenes.wrong: Ignore it and hope it recovers.
scenes.right: Set up alerts and retrain or roll back the model fast.
scenes.say: If your model's accuracy drops, don't just hope it bounces back. Interviewers want to hear that you monitor, alert, and retrain or roll back quickly.
